newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs close mixed, pork bellies mostly up.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs close mixed, pork bellies mostly up.

text.p: CME hog futures drifted late and closed mixed on a lack of fundamental direction with funds buying against mixed selling, traders said. Fund buying boosted pork bellies to higher levels late but the gains were trimmed as locals sold again at the close.

Hog futures closed 0.400 cent per lb lower to 0.125 higher with April off most at 74.075 cents. Bellies ended 0.225 cent lower to 0.250 higher with March up 0.125 at 82.100 and only May off at 83.725 cents.
Steady to weak cash hog prices Monday and expectations of a similar soft tone to the market Tuesday weighed on nearby hog futures, sources said.

But the market lacked strong direction and traders said "no one knows what to do." Funds typically buy on dips, especially after futures held technical support early and commercials were on both sides of the market awaiting a definite direction to cash hog prices this week, they said.
Packers have adequate hog supplies to start the week but their numbers may tighten later in the week if producers show resistance to their bids, traders added.
Pork cutout values rose $4.77 per cwt last week to highest levels since January 29.
The latest CME lean hog index was up $0.38 at $71.15 per cwt.

Rand Financials bought along with Rosenthal Collins after selling early. Lind-Waldock and R.J. O'Brien also sold April. Spreaders bought June and sold April Lind-Waldock and RBH bought July. In hog options, R.J. O'Brien sold June 74 puts and volitility was unchanged, pit sources added.

Pork bellies rose again late as fund buying offset light resistance. Early selling lacked outside follow through. Locals sold May at the close to turn that month down again by the closing bell, traders said.

Some analysts said the fresh belly market is finding resistance as high prices prompt end users to back away from the market. However, others looked for only a small near-term setback in values as they cited light stored stocks.
Cash belly prices were quoted by USDA down $1 per cwt at noon after rising late last week to highest levels since January 29.
E.D.&F. Man, Iowa Grain and LIT division of First Options bought May late, pit sources said.
